newsitem.title: FRANCE: Perez de Cuellar wants hostage-takers punished.
newsitem.headline: Perez de Cuellar wants hostage-takers punished.

text.p: Peruvian former U.N. secretary general Javier Perez de Cuellar said in an interview published in Paris on Wednesday that the Marxist hostage-takers at the Japanese embassy in Lima should be punished.

"One has to keep in mind that there are 140 hostages' lives at stake but a solution without a punishment for the hostage-takers would be difficult to admit," Perez de Cuellar told the newspaper Le Figaro.

The former U.N. chief, who stood unsuccessfully against Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori in 1995, said he was "not a friend" of the current government but praised Fujimori for taking what he called the right stance of firmness.
Perez de Cuellar said he believed a majority of Peruvians would favour police attacking the hostage-takers to force a solution "but I am against this because it could lead to an absurd butchery".
He added that the case demonstrated the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas "were incapable of joining the process of democracy".

The guerrillas, seeking freedom for more than 400 confederates in Peruvian jails, stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence during a reception last Tuesday, initally taking around 500 hostages. Many have since been released.
